program.section_heading: Foundations for Academic Success - Non-Credit COC (CDCP)

outcomes: Create a personal toolbox of reference materials and critical thinking strategies to enhance academic success
Reflect on one's learning processes and challenges
Develop an understanding of critical reading strategies in order to sustain the effort required for college level work.
Select and apply appropriate study skills to college coursework.
Evaluate and analyze print and online resources related to the attitudes and behaviors of successful college students.
Analyze personal values and strengths to set meaningful goals for life beyond community college.
Apply planning strategies and campus resources to build a next-step plan.
Develop a toolkit that supports confidence, readiness, and success in future academic and personal goals.
Develop a project that aligns with personal values, goals, and academic or career interests while addressing a campus or community need.
Implement the project using effective communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills that support success in future academic and professional settings.
Translate project insights into professional and academic materials that articulate strengths, purpose, and planned next steps in your educational and career pathway.

notes: The catalog labels the totals 'credits' (192.0 - 284.0 credits; 60 - 90 etc. per course), but this is a noncredit Certificate of Competency (CDCP), so the figures are read as hours and measure is set to 'hours'. Reviewer should confirm.

The 'Program Outcomes' heading prints outcomes grouped under each course (COLL 0600 through COLL 0603) rather than program-level outcomes; they are recorded in course_outcomes under the codes as printed there (with a space, e.g. 'COLL 0600'), and program.outcomes is left empty. Reviewer may consider them program outcomes instead.
The block's stated total 192 - 284 is the 'Program Requirements Complete (Total 192 - 284)' figure, which covers this single block.
The Recommended Sequence (Term 1-4) repeats the same four required courses and is not recorded as a separate block.
No careers are named in the text.
